identity.description: Glass-box linear scorer: operator-defined factors, each passed through a declared normalizer (percentile/minmax/zscore/logistic/banded/lookup, with a HigherIsBetter direction), combined by hand-set OR fitted weights into a single score, optionally banded into tiers. Every prediction decomposes EXACTLY into per-factor contributions — the weights are the whole story.

axes.learningTypeNote: Supervised applies to the trainable (weight-fitting) mode; the hand-weighted mode learns nothing and never sees a target

consumes.note: target is OPTIONAL — required only when fit_weights=true (trainable mode); a hand-weighted rubric scores with no target ever seen. Categorical factors are consumed via the lookup/banded normalizers, not one-hot encoding.

emits.note: the weighted composite — the primary output in both modes
banded tiers: the score cut at operator-defined band_edges (e.g. Bronze/Silver/Gold, A–F)
the factor weights themselves; standard errors exist ONLY in fitted mode — hand-set weights carry no SE

EXACT: weight × normalized factor value reproduces the score identically — no SHAP approximation needed. This exactness is the family's distinguishing strength over models whose attributions are estimated.

learnsVsFixed.why: THE exerciser of reusable≠trainable: a hand-weighted rubric is a REUSABLE-ONLY (untrained) instance — deployable with zero training rows; setting fit_weights=true turns the SAME component into a trainable one whose weights come from a constrained linear fit. Weight SEARCH (exploring weight vectors against an objective) is a wave-strategist concern layered on top — noted here, deliberately not modeled as a component behavior.

factors.prior: not-searched (operator-authored structure: per-factor {name, source_column, normalizer ∈ percentile|minmax|zscore|logistic|banded|lookup, higher_is_better, normalizer_params})

weights.prior: not-searched (hand-set by the operator OR fitted; searching the weight vector is a wave-strategist concern, not a per-model HP dimension)

fit_weights.prior: not-searched (mode switch: false = reusable-only hand-weighted instance, true = trainable constrained-linear fit)

non_negative.prior: not-searched (constraint honoring the rubric's declared factor directions)

band_edges.default: quantile terciles of the scored distribution
band_edges.prior: not-searched (operator-defined tier boundaries; presentation, not fit)

invariances.why: a weighted sum changes with any factor rescale — which is exactly why every factor is REQUIRED to pass through a declared normalizer before combination
only the percentile normalizer is rank-based; under minmax/zscore/logistic a monotone transform of a raw factor changes its normalized value and hence the score
a missing factor value makes the weighted sum undefined; each factor needs imputation or a declared default sub-score before combination
the lookup and banded normalizers map category levels / value ranges directly to factor sub-scores — the scorecard tradition's binning, no one-hot needed
the scorer is a deterministic linear combination with no error model; only the fitted mode's OPTIONAL standard errors lean on linear-model assumptions
hand-weighted mode needs ZERO training rows by construction; fitted mode is a low-variance constrained linear fit that stabilizes from tens of rows
the normalizers saturate or clamp outside their calibration range (percentile→[0,1], logistic asymptotes, minmax/banded clamp), so the composite score stays bounded even though the combiner is linear

featureStats.why: unnormalized mixed-scale factors let the largest-scale factor silently dominate the weighted sum — the signal that triggers the mandatory-normalization bank entry
two highly correlated factors double-count one underlying signal in a plain weighted sum, inflating its effective weight beyond what either declared weight says
a missing factor voids the sum (no native NaN), so per-factor missingness drives the impute-or-declared-default policy before any scoring

modelMetrics.why: mean |weight × normalized value| share per factor IS the exact additive decomposition of the score — read directly, not approximated — and one factor owning it flags a degenerate rubric or leakage
a fitted weight whose sign contradicts the factor's declared HigherIsBetter direction means the data disagrees with the rubric's stated semantics — a promotion gate, not a silent flip
the distance between fitted weights and the operator's hand weights quantifies how much the data disputes the rubric's priors — the core trainable-mode diagnostic

edgeCases.behavior: score identically 0 for every record; ranking undefined

edgeCases.condition: unnormalized mixed-scale factors (normalizer omitted/identity on raw inputs)
edgeCases.behavior: largest-scale factor dominates the sum regardless of declared weights

edgeCases.condition: fitted weight sign conflicts with the factor's declared HigherIsBetter direction
edgeCases.behavior: per-factor contributions contradict the rubric's stated semantics

edgeCases.condition: unseen category level at score time under a lookup normalizer with no declared default
edgeCases.behavior: no mapped sub-score; the record is unscorable

edgeCases.condition: a factor with zero variance (constant across records)
edgeCases.behavior: burns weight budget with zero discrimination; contributes only a constant offset; may signal leakage or a data-quality issue

driver.constructor: RubricWeightedScorecard(factors, weights=None, fit_weights=False, non_negative=True, fit_loss='logistic', l2_penalty=0.0, band_edges=None)
driver.wrapperNeeds: thin custom wrapper — hand-weighted mode must expose a no-op fit() while keeping sklearn-style predict/score; fitted mode maps the sign/non-negativity constraints onto sklearn.linear_model (positive=True plus direction-flip preprocessing)
driver.threadSafety: predict is a pure vectorized dot product — fully thread-safe; fit is single-threaded

placementClaims.why: no native NaN: a missing factor voids the weighted sum, so every factor needs imputation or a declared default sub-score upstream
the rubric's non-linear normalizers (percentile, logistic, banded, lookup) LIVE at this position — this claim references them; the sheet does not duplicate them as model internals
the minmax/zscore normalizers live here; scale-sensitive by mechanism — a weighted sum over unnormalized mixed-scale factors is dominated by the largest-scale factor
the lookup/banded normalizers consume category levels directly; one-hot encoding would fracture a single rubric factor into many weight-fragments and break the one-factor-one-weight story
